# infrawrench_pr_check_repository (Resource)

Pull request checks on one GitHub repository: on every new commit of an open pull request, Infrawrench posts a check run with the estimated monthly cost change of the Terraform it adds, edits or removes, the blast radius of every existing resource it touches, and right-sizing, tag policy and posture warnings.

Checks are posted by the organization's GitHub App, as the app, so there is no token here. The repository is named by the `installation_id` of a GitHub App installation connected to the organization plus its `owner/name`; both come from the organization's `/github/repos` listing (the repository picker under **Settings, Pull Request Checks** reads the same list). The installation must have approved the app's **Checks: read and write**, **Pull requests: read** (read and write for `comment_enabled`) and **Contents: read** permissions; the settings page shows which are missing.

Existing resources are matched through the Terraform state uploaded to IaC reconciliation, so a repository whose state has not been uploaded gets cost estimates from the code alone and no blast radius for edits.

Reading needs `iac:read`; changing anything needs `org:settings:write`. `terraform destroy` turns the checks off and deletes the repository's check history; checks already posted on GitHub stay there.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Installation ids and repository names come from the organization's
# `/github/repos` listing (the same list the repository picker in
# Settings > Pull Request Checks shows).
resource "infrawrench_pr_check_repository" "infra" {
  installation_id = 51234567
  repository      = "acme/infra"

  # Keep one summary comment on each infrastructure pull request.
  comment_enabled = true

  # Fail the check (blocking merge where it is required) when a pull request
  # adds more than 500 a month.
  cost_threshold       = 500
  threshold_conclusion = "failure"

  # Only look at the production root modules.
  directories = ["terraform/prod", "terraform/shared"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `installation_id` (Number) The GitHub App installation that reaches `repository`, as listed by `/github/repos`.
- `repository` (String) The repository, as `owner/name`, 3-201 characters. One resource per repository: a second resource naming the same repository is refused.

### Optional

- `comment_enabled` (Boolean) Also keep one summary comment on each pull request that changes infrastructure, edited in place on every push rather than posted again. Defaults to false.
- `cost_threshold` (Number) Monthly cost increase, between 0 and 10000000 in the estimate's currency (USD for every provider that prices today), above which the check concludes `threshold_conclusion` instead of success. Omit it for no threshold. An increase that could not be priced never trips it.
- `directories` (List of String) Path prefixes the check looks in, up to 20, each 1-255 characters, without leading or trailing slashes (`infra/prod`). Empty, the default, covers the whole repository.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Post checks on this repository's pull requests. Defaults to true; false keeps the settings without posting.
- `threshold_conclusion` (String) What the check concludes above `cost_threshold`: `neutral` (the default) flags it without blocking, `failure` fails the check, which blocks merging where branch protection requires it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned id. Use it with `terraform import`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imports under the repository's pull request check id, shown in the
# `/pr-checks/repositories` listing.
terraform import infrawrench_pr_check_repository.infra 0b5c2a7e-1f3d-4c6a-9e8b-2d4f6a8c0e1f
```
